cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Generalize – To make a broad, sweeping statement by inferring from specific cases.

p.em: Example: Instead of processing one bad date, we decided to generalize about three billion men.

cosy-blockquote.p: Satire – The use of humor, irony, or exaggeration to expose and criticize absurdity.

p.em: Example: The song is a brilliant satire of late-night alcohol-fueled group vent sessions.

cosy-blockquote.p: Condescending – Having or showing a feeling of patronizing superiority.

p.em: Example: He gave a condescending explanation about a topic she had a PhD in.

cosy-blockquote.p: Repressed – Restrained, inhibited, or oppressed, especially regarding emotions.

p.em: Example: Ranting about exes is a classic way to release years of repressed frustration.

cosy-blockquote.p: Anger – A strong feeling of annoyance, displeasure, or hostility.

p.em: Example: Her righteous anger was quickly converted into an upbeat 80s pop dance routine.

cosy-blockquote.p: Blanket – Covering all cases or classes; total and indiscriminate.

p.em: Example: Issuing a blanket condemnation of an entire gender is scientifically flawed but cathartic.

cosy-blockquote.p: Conflate – To combine two or more texts, ideas, or individuals into one.

p.em: Example: It is easy to conflate bad personal choices with universal human flaws.

cosy-blockquote.p: Exception – A person or thing that is excluded from a general statement.

p.em: Example: They intentionally ignored every good guy as an unhelpful exception to their rule.

cosy-blockquote.p: Distinguish – To recognize or point out a difference between items or people.

p.em: Example: When you are furious, you rarely bother to distinguish nuance from malice.

cosy-blockquote.p: Nuance – A subtle difference in or shade of meaning, expression, or sound.

p.em: Example: Nuance completely disappears the moment a group anthem starts.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: Let's generalize for all men → Correct: Let's generalize about all men ((Use the preposition 'about' after 'generalize'.))
Incorrect: They conflate his mistake with all the humanity → Correct: They conflate his mistake with universal flaws ((Use 'conflate A with B' without unnecessary articles.))
Incorrect: He is an exception of the rule → Correct: He is an exception to the rule ((Use the fixed prepositional phrase 'exception to the rule'.))
